lines.text: A wife of noble character is far more precious than rubies, and she brings her husband good all her days.
She works with eager hands, is like the merchant ships, rises while it is still night, and buys a field.
Her lamp is not extinguished at night, she opens her arms to the kings, and her household is clothed in scarlet.
Her husband sits among the elders at the temple courts, and she sells linen garments and wears strength and honor.
Her children call her blessed, and the poem says a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
